name: Bridge outbound: messenger message to WhatsApp (event sink)
description:
## Context
Messages written by team users in the codx-junior chat (the "messenger" side) must be forwarded to the linked WhatsApp group/DM. `EventManager.message_event` is already the single funnel for message updates, so a small sink registry covers live messages without touching `ChatEngine`.

## Objective
Outbound fan-out with loop prevention and WhatsApp-safe formatting.

## Steps
1. `codx/junior/events/event_manager.py`: class-level sink registry — `register_sink(fn)` / `unregister_sink(fn)`, invoked from `message_event()` (and `chat_event()` for system notices) inside `try/except` so a failing channel never breaks the AI loop.
2. `codx/junior/channels/sink.py` — `WhatsAppSink.on_message(chat, message)`:
   - skip unless an enabled binding exists for `chat.id` with `direction in (out, both)`;
   - skip messages carrying `meta_data.channel` for that same binding (echo/loop prevention), `hide`, `task_item`, `role == "error"`, and empty content;
   - role filter per policy (user messages always; assistant messages only when bot mode is on);
   - format + split, then send through `WhatsAppClient` with `recipient_type="group"` for groups and `"individual"` for DMs;
   - record sent external ids in the binding ledger to keep idempotency and debugging.
3. `codx/junior/channels/formatting.py`:
   - Markdown → WhatsApp (`**b**`→`*b*`, `*i*`→`_i_`, `~~s~~`→`~s~`, headings → bold line, lists kept, tables rendered as aligned text or bullet pairs, links kept as raw URLs);
   - split at ≤ 4096 chars on paragraph boundaries and never inside a code fence; `[1/3]` prefixes on multi-part sends.
4. Register the sink from the channels bootstrap (called on app startup / background service start) with failures logged.

## Files
- codx/junior/events/event_manager.py
- codx/junior/channels/sink.py (new)
- codx/junior/channels/formatting.py (new)
- tests/channels/test_formatting.py (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A user message typed in the messenger appears in the linked WhatsApp group as the configured team user.
- [ ] Messages mirrored FROM WhatsApp are never sent back (no echo, no infinite loop).
- [ ] Long answers are split into ordered ≤4096-char parts, code fences preserved.
- [ ] Markdown tables/headings render readably in WhatsApp.
- [ ] A channel failure is logged and does not interrupt the chat turn.
